messages.subject_clean: [methylkit_discussion] adjusting colors in clustersamples and pcasamples in methylkit
messages.body_plain:
colors are default. the PCA function returns the PCA invisibly. You can get the PCA coordinates from that and do a scatter plot yourself.

pcs=PCASamples(methylBase.obj)
loads = pcs$rotation
plot(loads[,1],loads[,2])

messages.body_plain:
if someone was interested to get their own color codes clustersamples:
c <- clusterSamples(meth, dist="correlation", method="ward", plot=F)
labelColors = c("#CD0000","#8B4789","#006400","#104E8B")
clusMember <- c("Ctrl1"=1, "Ctrl2"=1,"Ctrl3"=1,"KO1"=2,"KO2"=2, "KO3"=2, "A1"=3,"A2"=3,"A3"=3, "A-KO1"=4, "A-KO2"=4, "A-KO3"=4)
# function to get color labels
colLab <- function(n) {
    if (is.leaf(n)) {
        a <- attributes(n)
        labCol <- labelColors[clusMember[which(names(clusMember) == a$label)]]
        attr(n, "nodePar") <- c(a$nodePar, lab.col = labCol)
    }
    n
}
# using dendrapply
clusDendro = dendrapply(as.dendrogram(c), colLab)
# make plot
plot(clusDendro, main = "CpG methylation Clustering")

####

messages.subject: Test of methylation variability between groups, as in diffVar of missMethyl
messages.subject_clean: Test of methylation variability between groups, as in diffVar of missMethyl
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have a RRBS data from 2 groups of 6 samples (6 mothers and 6 daughters, genetically related one-to-one).
I was wondering if there is a way to compare the variability in methylation of all CpGs between the two groups just with methylKit, similar to what is proposed by diffVar function of missMethyl.
In fact, my hypothesis is that one group should show higher variability in methylation, no matter the mean methylation level or the significance of methylation differences.

Thank you in advance for any suggestion,

tom

messages.subject: Incorporating Imputation into MethylKit's analysis pipeline
messages.subject_clean: Incorporating Imputation into MethylKit's analysis pipeline
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I was wondering if MethylKit is capable of analysing lower-depth WGBS datasets that have had any missing methylation values imputed?

I've experimented with using MethIMPUTE, which produces a methylation level for missing values - but the unite() function produces an object that uses coverage values, which would remain as 0 for imputed values, whereas the methylation value would be changed.

Does anyone use imputation in their analysis with MethylKit? And if so, what is your recommended best practice in incorporating it into your analysis pipeline?

Best,

Dean

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Incorporating Imputation into MethylKit's analysis pipeline
messages.subject_clean: [methylkit_discussion] Incorporating Imputation into MethylKit's analysis pipeline
messages.body_plain:
This can be done but needs a bit of work. If you use k-nearest neighbor method for imputation you can use methylation ratios to calculate k-nearest neighbors then use the same neighbors to calculate coverage value as mean of coverage values from nearest neighbors, rounded to the nearest integer. Then you can work out number of Cs and Ts from the imputed methylation ratio.

How many samples do you have ? Is this single-cell data?

Best
Altuna

If you use k-nearest neighbor method for imputation you can use methylation ratios to calculate k-nearest neighbors then use the same neighbors to calculate coverage value as mean of coverage values from nearest neighbors, rounded to the nearest integer.
